comment: The text repeatedly warns that a central bus creates a single point of control or failure. A properly engineered central or clustered service can provide redundancy, governance, and consistent enforcement, while distributed architectures can also concentrate control through central trust services or registries.

public.text: The text repeatedly warns that a central bus creates a single point of control or failure. A properly engineered central or clustered service can provide redundancy, governance, and consistent enforcement, while distributed architectures can also concentrate control through central trust services or registries.
public.suggestedRevision: Present the risks as design-dependent rather than inherent. Compare centralised, distributed, and hybrid patterns using governance, resilience, scalability, observability, security, cost, and operational-capacity criteria.
